units.claim_summary: Ganesha is presented as the accessible divine child through whom devotees can approach Shiva and Parvati as the universal parents.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குழந்தை வழியே உலகப் பெற்றோரிடம்?

units.claim_summary: Devotion to Ganesha should combine reverence with affectionate intimacy, because he is approached both as deity and as beloved child of the divine household.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பயத்தோடு, ப்ரியத்தோடு?

units.claim_summary: Ganesha worship is deliberately portrayed as easy and widely available, requiring neither elaborate resources nor exclusive ritual settings.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எளிதில் கிடைப்பவர்?

units.claim_summary: Ganesha’s familial greatness is illustrated through the prestige of his divine ancestry, while that pedigree is used devotionally rather than as an independent proof of divinity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாட்டனார் பெருமை?

units.claim_summary: Vishnu’s relationship to Ganesha as maternal uncle is used to enlarge the devotional picture of Ganesha’s place within the divine family.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மாமா மஹிமை?

units.claim_summary: The sibling relationship traditionally drawn between Vishnu and the Goddess is used to connect Vaishnava and Shakta-Shaiva forms of worship within one divine kinship.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருமாலும் அம்பிகையும்?

units.claim_summary: A traditional story of Vishnu humbling himself before Ganesha is used to teach that even exalted deities honor the remover of obstacles before undertaking important work.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருமால் செய்த கோணங்கி?

units.claim_summary: The familiar Suklambaradharam verse is interpreted as an invocation of Ganesha, showing how conventional epithets can function within a specific ritual tradition despite lexical ambiguity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “சுக்லாம்பரதரம்”?

units.claim_summary: Praise of Ganesha’s parents culminates in the claim that the son who embodies their greatness is himself worthy of direct salutation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பெற்றோர் பெருமை?

units.claim_summary: Ganesha’s status as Muruga’s elder brother is used to reinforce his precedence in worship, while his worth is not reduced to family seniority alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முருகனும் மூத்தோனும்?

units.claim_summary: Ganesha deserves reverence for his own divine qualities and not merely because he belongs to an illustrious divine family.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மரியாதைக்குரிய குழந்தை?

units.claim_summary: Ganesha may be worshipped as the supreme divine reality itself, not only as the son of Shiva and Parvati.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முழுமுதற் கடவுளாக?

units.claim_summary: The Tripura narrative is used to teach that even Shiva’s undertaking is said to fail when Ganesha is not first invoked, and to succeed after the omission is repaired.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தந்தை பூஜித்த தனயர்?

units.claim_summary: A modern Rameswaram incident is narrated as a devotional parallel to the older Ganesha-obstacle tradition; it is presented as testimony, not independently verified history.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸமீபகால ஸம்பவத்தில் புராண நிருபணம்?

units.claim_summary: The Lalitopakhyana episode portrays Ganesha as destroying an obstructive magical device and restoring the Goddess’s forces, a supernatural narrative supporting his obstacle-removing role.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அன்னைக்கு உதவிய ஐங்கரன்?

units.claim_summary: Traditions about Muruga’s renunciation and marriage depict Ganesha as the elder brother whose intervention shapes the younger deity’s story.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முருகனுக்குதவிய முன்னவன்?

units.claim_summary: Rama and other Vishnu-associated traditions are cited as worshipping Ganesha, supporting the claim that Ganesha invocation crosses sectarian devotional boundaries.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ராமபிரானும் விநாயகரும்?

units.claim_summary: The Syamantaka narrative is introduced as the scriptural setting for explaining Krishna’s accusation, vindication, and later connection with Ganesha-Chaturthi observance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்யமந்தகத்தின் கதை?

units.claim_summary: The Syamantaka jewel’s solar origin is used to connect the narrative with Surya worship before its later Ganesha-related devotional interpretation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸூர்யனும் விநாயகரும்?

units.claim_summary: The Syamantaka jewel is said to have been obtained through intense worship of Surya, presenting extraordinary possession as the fruit of tapas within the narrative.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தவத்தால் பெற்ற திவ்யமணி?

units.claim_summary: Krishna’s refusal to covet the Syamantaka jewel is presented as an example of detachment even in the presence of extraordinary wealth.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கண்ணனின் வைராக்யம்?

units.claim_summary: Jambavan’s role in the Syamantaka story is narrated to connect Krishna’s search for the jewel with an older Ramayana-associated devotee.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜாம்பவான்?

units.claim_summary: Krishna’s involvement with the missing Syamantaka jewel shows how even an innocent and exalted person can become the target of public suspicion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஐயத்துக்கு ஆளான ஐயன்?

units.claim_summary: Krishna responds to accusation by investigating the Syamantaka affair and tracing the evidence rather than relying only on status or assertion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கண்ணன் துப்பறிந்தார்?

units.claim_summary: Recovery of the Syamantaka jewel becomes intertwined with marriage alliances, showing how the object drives both vindication and new social relationships in the story.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மணியும் பெண்மணியும்?

units.claim_summary: Krishna’s combat with Jambavan is narrated as ending in recognition through physical encounter, turning conflict into devotional identification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சண்டையில் ஸ்பரிச இன்பம்?

units.claim_summary: The Syamantaka jewel narrative is shown as leading to multiple marriages, illustrating how one disputed possession generates wider narrative consequences.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மணியில் விளைந்த திருமணங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The story links rivalry over a woman and marriage alliance with hostility surrounding the Syamantaka jewel, warning how attachment can generate conflict.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பெண்ணால் விளைந்த பகைமை?

units.claim_summary: Krishna repeatedly clears himself of blame yet becomes vulnerable to renewed accusation, emphasizing the persistence of public suspicion around the jewel.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மீண்டும் வெற்றி, மீண்டும் பழி?

units.claim_summary: Akrura’s connection with the Syamantaka jewel is introduced as the next stage in resolving the jewel’s disappearance and the accusations attached to it.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அக்ரூரம் மணியும்?

units.claim_summary: The discourse traces Krishna’s accusation to the chain of possession and suspicion around the Syamantaka jewel rather than treating blame as causeless.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அபவாதத்துக்குக் காரணம்?

units.claim_summary: Differences between lunar and solar calendrical systems are used to explain why Bhadrapada/Ganesha observance dates can appear to vary across panchangas.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாத்ரபதம்; பஞ்சாங்க வித்யாஸம்?

units.claim_summary: The Ganesha-moon legend portrays the moon’s pride as being broken by a curse, using mythic narrative to condemn ridicule and vanity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சந்திரனின் கர்வ பங்கம்?

units.claim_summary: The inner purpose of the moon-curse story is interpreted as moral correction rather than arbitrary divine anger.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சாபத்தின் உட்கிடை?

units.claim_summary: Ganesha’s modification of the moon’s curse is presented as compassionate relief when its consequences would otherwise burden the wider world.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சாப விமோசனம்?

units.claim_summary: The crescent moon associated with Shiva and Ganesha is interpreted within the tradition as part of the reconciliation following the moon-curse episode.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “பால சந்த்ரன்”?

units.claim_summary: Sankatahara Chaturthi is presented as a merciful observance through which devotees seek relief from obstacles and the effects associated with the moon-curse tradition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸங்கடஹர சதுர்த்தி?

units.claim_summary: Krishna’s connection with the moon is used to bring the Syamantaka accusation story into the Ganesha-Chaturthi observance tradition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கண்ணனும் சந்த்ரனும்?

units.claim_summary: The prescribed sighting of the third-day moon is presented in the tradition as a ritual remedy for the danger of false accusation linked with the Chaturthi legend.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அபவாதம் நீங்க வரம்!?

units.claim_summary: Divine-avatar stories of suffering and accusation are interpreted as serving public welfare by creating teachings and observances useful to later devotees.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about லீலையின் பயன் லோகக்ஷேமம்?

units.claim_summary: Krishna’s release from the Syamantaka accusation is tied devotionally to Ganesha worship, completing the narrative explanation for the associated observance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அபவாத நீக்கம்?

units.claim_summary: The seasonal proximity of Krishna Jayanti and Ganesha Chaturthi is used to connect the two devotional cycles through the Syamantaka-moon narrative.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜயந்திகளின் விசேஷம்?

units.claim_summary: Guru, acharya, and teacher are distinguished by function and usage, with the traditional educational vocabulary showing that spiritual guidance is broader than classroom instruction.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு, ஆசார்யர், வாத்தியார்?

units.claim_summary: The vocabulary of lesson and study is traced to Vedic learning, presenting later educational practice as rooted in the older oral-scriptural tradition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேதத் தொடர்பு?

units.claim_summary: Traditional texts distinguish the upadhyaya who teaches for livelihood from the acharya who transmits an entire discipline as a dharmic responsibility.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உபாத்யாயரும் ஆசார்யரும்?

units.claim_summary: Teaching undertaken principally as a livelihood is contrasted with the older ideal of education as a duty and relationship not reducible to commercial exchange.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about போதனை ஜீவனோபாயமாக?

units.claim_summary: Guru and acharya overlap as guides but are not always identical categories; dharma texts distinguish their roles according to initiation, teaching, and formation of the student.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு-ஆசார்ய ஒற்றுமை-வேற்றுமை?

units.claim_summary: Residential gurukula life is valued because continuous life with the teacher can shape conduct and discipline in ways that instruction within the parental home cannot.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வீட்டில் இல்லாத குருகுலச் சிறப்பம்சம்?

units.claim_summary: Mother, father, and teacher are all assigned exceptional reverence, with traditional rankings used to emphasize gratitude for birth, upbringing, and knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தாய் – தந்தையர் பெருமை?

units.claim_summary: A teacher may be younger in age yet spiritually or intellectually senior, because knowledge rather than chronological age determines the relevant form of reverence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வயதில் சிறிய குரு?

units.claim_summary: The traditional hierarchy of mother, father, and teacher is used to teach that betrayal of those foundational relationships carries especially grave moral consequences.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அன்னை – தந்தை – ஆசான்?

units.claim_summary: Although upadhyaya originally marked a livelihood-oriented teaching role, later usage elevated it into an honorific, illustrating semantic change in educational titles.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “உபாத்யாயர்” பெற்ற உயர்வு?

units.claim_summary: Traditional vocation and teaching are presented as forms of service to Ishvara when performed according to inherited dharma; the varna framework is a context-sensitive normative claim.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வர ஆராதனையாக?

units.claim_summary: The Brahmin’s listed duties are used to argue that accepting gifts is not meant to become unrestricted dependence and that teaching compensation should not be treated as a commercial fee.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “ஏற்பது இகழ்ச்சி”?

units.claim_summary: The Indian acharya ideal is presented as distinctive because the teacher’s personal discipline and way of life are part of what is transmitted, not merely information.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிற நாடுகளில் இல்லாத சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Teachers of worldly arts and sciences are also expected to embody discipline and character, extending the acharya ideal beyond explicitly religious subjects.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உலகியல் படிப்பிலும் உத்தம ஆசார்யர்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The title kulapati denotes the exceptional head of a large residential scholarly community and should not be confused with an ordinary household teacher.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “குலபதி”?

units.claim_summary: Early education is portrayed as beginning in rishi households and expanding from family-based transmission into wider institutions and scholarly lineages.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பூர்வகால போதனையமைப்பின் வளர்ச்சி?

units.claim_summary: Attention to language, sound, accent, and grammar is presented as integral to Vedic learning because accurate oral transmission depends on disciplined phonetic form.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மொழி, ஒலி ஒழுங்கு?

units.claim_summary: The absence of writing in early Vedic education is presented as compatible with rigorous preservation through memorization, while education is said to aim at transformation rather than income.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எழுத்தில்லாத போதனை!?

units.claim_summary: Terms such as kula, shakha, satra, and charana are used to trace the growth of learning from family lineages into broader Vedic study communities; the social history remains context-sensitive.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குலம், சாகை, சாத்ரன், சரணம் முதலியன?

units.claim_summary: Guru-dakshina is presented as a voluntary expression of gratitude after learning, not as a pre-negotiated wage that turns knowledge into a commodity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குருதக்ஷிணை?

units.claim_summary: Ancient arts and sciences are treated as genuine vidyas, yet the Narada example is used to argue that extensive secular knowledge does not by itself produce final spiritual fulfillment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பூர்வகாலக் கலைகளும் ஸயன்ஸ்களும்?

units.claim_summary: Dharma orders embodied and social life through right action, while Brahman-knowledge concerns final liberation; disciplined dharmic life is presented as preparation rather than the final end.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தர்மம் – ப்ரஹ்மம்?

units.claim_summary: Even rival or heterodox systems were studied within the broad intellectual world of Vedic education, which is presented as capacious enough to examine opposing views rather than ignore them.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வைதிகமாகவே ஸகல வித்யைகளும்?

units.claim_summary: Gurukula education is described as including students from multiple varnas with differentiated curricula; this is a traditional social claim requiring caste context rather than modern endorsement.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எல்லா ஜாதியாரும்?

units.claim_summary: Education is presented as a social obligation rather than an optional luxury, with society expected to ensure that children receive formation appropriate to their capacities and duties.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கட்டாய கல்வி?

units.claim_summary: Instruction should be matched to the student’s aptitude and readiness rather than imposed uniformly, because education succeeds only when the recipient is a suitable vessel for the teaching.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாத்திரமறிந்து?

units.claim_summary: Later educational changes are criticized for separating learning from discipline, livelihood from service, and knowledge from moral formation, producing what the discourse sees as modern distortion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிற்கால மாறுதலும் தற்கால விபரீதமும்?

units.claim_summary: The maxim about hearing truth from whoever speaks it is used to defend intellectual openness: a claim should be judged by its truth rather than by the identity of its speaker.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “யாரார் வாய் கேட்பினும்”?

units.claim_summary: Open-minded reception of truth is paired with discrimination, so receptivity to many teachers does not mean abandoning standards of truth or disciplined judgment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இன்னோர் உண்மை?

units.claim_summary: Giving knowledge is ranked as an especially high form of charity because it equips the recipient with a durable capacity rather than a temporary material benefit.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வித்யாதானத்தின் உயர்வு?

units.claim_summary: Traditional educational stages and durations are presented as deliberate structures for gradual formation, not arbitrary extensions of schooling.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கல்வித் திட்டத்தில் கால அளவைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Householders are assigned an educational role because a stable social order must support students, teachers, and transmission rather than leaving learning only to renunciants.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about க்ருஹஸ்தர்களுக்கு ஏன்??

units.claim_summary: Traditional school holidays are explained as serving ritual, health, and educational rhythms rather than being merely breaks from study.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விடுமுறை நாட்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Physical punishment of students is treated as tightly constrained and subordinate to the aim of correction; cruelty or anger is not presented as legitimate teaching discipline.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மாணவனை அடிக்கலாமா??

units.claim_summary: The ideal student is described through humility, effort, restraint, attentiveness, and willingness to serve, making character part of readiness for learning.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மாணவன் லக்ஷணம்?

units.claim_summary: Traditional education is presented as attending to bodily health and balanced development so that study does not become detached from the student’s physical well-being.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆரோக்ய வளர்ச்சிக்கும் உதவி?

units.claim_summary: Personal instruction by a responsible teacher is preferred because the teacher can know the student’s character, capacity, and progress in a way an impersonal institution cannot.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தனிப்பட்ட ஆசான் பெருமை?

units.claim_summary: Large educational institutions are criticized for weakening the intimate teacher-student relationship, even when institutions become practically necessary for organizing learning.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்தாபனத்தின் குறைபாடு?

units.claim_summary: Upanishadic examples are used to show teachers and students speaking with unusual openness, making honest questioning and disclosure part of genuine spiritual education.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உள்ளம் திறந்து குரு – சிஷ்யர்கள் உபநிஷத உதாரணங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Shraddha and persistent questioning are presented as complementary: trust enables learning, while sincere inquiry prevents passive or superficial acceptance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ச்ரத்தை; பரிப்ரச்நம்?

units.claim_summary: A teacher may test and refine a disciple before giving deeper instruction, because readiness for knowledge includes character and endurance as well as intelligence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சோதித்துத் துலக்குவது?

units.claim_summary: The guru’s wife is included within the sphere of reverence and service in residential education because the gurukula functions as a household community rather than a classroom alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு பத்னி?

units.claim_summary: Even when divine powers or extraordinary teachers appear in a student’s education, the student’s loyalty to the human guru is not to be displaced.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தெய்வசக்திகள் போதித்தாலும் குருபக்தி குறையாதது?

units.claim_summary: Instruction may be given in stages and through tests that force the student to think independently, so disciplined obedience is not meant to suppress reflection.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பரீக்ஷை செய்து படிப்படியாக உபதேசம்; மாணவனின் ஸ்வய சிந்தனைக்கு ஊக்கம்?

units.claim_summary: The Krishna-Kuchela school narrative is used to portray the teacher’s affection and responsibility for students as extending beyond formal lessons.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கண்ணன் கதையில் ஆசானின் அன்புடைமை?

units.claim_summary: A good disciple also helps form the guru by eliciting responsibility, self-discipline, and careful teaching; the educational relationship is therefore reciprocal in moral effect.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குருலக்ஷணம்: குருவை சிஷ்யன் உரு செய்வது?

units.claim_summary: The same reciprocal responsibility applies to an institutional guru-seat: disciples and institutional expectations can strengthen or distort the person who occupies it.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு பீடத்துக்கும் பொருந்தும்?

units.claim_summary: A solitary renunciate and the head of a teaching institution face different obligations, because institutional leadership necessarily creates responsibilities toward disciples and society.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தனித்துறவியும், பீடகுருவும்?

units.claim_summary: Religious institutions are called a practical necessity despite their dangers, especially after large Buddhist and Jain institutions made organized teaching and social work unavoidable; the historical comparison remains attributed.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்தாபனம் “அவச்யத் தீமை”க்கு ஆசார்யாள் பணி?

units.claim_summary: Ancient centers such as Taxila and other large schools are cited to show that India had major residential institutions long before the modern university model; individual historical details require external verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பழங்காலக் கல்விப் பெருநிலையங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Buddhist and Jain traditions are described as developing large educational establishments partly for organized teaching and missionary purposes, a historical-interreligious claim requiring context.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about புது மதங்களும் பெரிய கல்வி நிலையங்களும்?

units.claim_summary: A special historical-social setting is offered to explain why some gurukulas became Brahmin-centered and why educational ages and curricula differed by social role; the varna framework is not generalized as a modern prescription.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “ப்ரத்யேகச் சூழ்நிலை”?

units.claim_summary: Traditional curricula are described as differing according to vocation and social role, with the claim presented as part of the historical varna-based educational order.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாடதிட்டத்தில் வேறுபாடுகள்?

units.claim_summary: The term kadigai is investigated philologically rather than assumed from later usage, introducing a source-based inquiry into the name of major traditional educational centers.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பெயர்க் காரணம்?

units.claim_summary: Inscriptions and older references are used to argue for the antiquity of kadigai institutions, while the historical dating remains dependent on those documentary witnesses.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கடிகையின் தொன்மை?

units.claim_summary: The rise of stone temples under the Pallavas is connected with the institutional setting in which temples and centers of learning became enduring public structures; the architectural chronology is historical evidence, not doctrinal teaching.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கற்கோயிலின் தோற்றம்?

units.claim_summary: Temple and kadigai are presented as complementary institutions, joining worship and advanced learning within the same cultural landscape.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கோயிலும் கடிகையும்?

units.claim_summary: Eighth-century inscriptional evidence is used to argue that kadigai institutions continued to enjoy substantial status and patronage after their earlier development.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எட்டாம் நூற்றாண்டில்?

units.claim_summary: A royal inscription is explained as having a conventional structure—praise, operative grant, and protective or imprecatory conclusion—so its parts must be read according to documentary function.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சாஸனத்தின் அமைப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Inscriptional references to kadigais with thousands of students are used to argue that some traditional educational centers were very large, while the discourse explicitly allows that numerical figures may be hyperbolic.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஏழாயிரம் மாணவர்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Inscriptions from Andhra and Karnataka are surveyed to show that institutions called kadigai were not confined to Kanchi but spread across southern regions over many centuries.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆந்திர, கர்நாடகங்களில்?

units.claim_summary: Chola-country evidence is used to show that substantial Vedic schools existed even where the institutional name kadigai was less common, marking a southern limit of that terminology rather than of learning itself.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சோழ நாட்டிலும்?

units.claim_summary: A Maharashtra-associated reference to kadigai is used to argue that the term and institution had prestige beyond Tamil and Karnataka regions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மஹாராஷ்டிரத்திலும் பெருமை?

units.claim_summary: The name kadigai is investigated through meanings connected with a pot and a unit of time, but superficial resemblance to a clock is rejected as insufficient explanation of the educational term.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கடிகைக்குக் கடிகாரத் தொடர்புண்டா??

units.claim_summary: Uses of kadigai in place names and in Nanmanikkadigai show that the word had several senses, so the school-name etymology must be established from context rather than assumed from one later meaning.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கடிகாசலம், நான்மணிக்கடிகை?

units.claim_summary: A Kumarila-related textual reference is used to push the claimed antiquity and geographic range of kadigasthana earlier and farther north, while the associated dating remains a historical claim requiring verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கி.மு. ஐந்தாம் நூற்றாண்டிலேயே; ப்ரயாகையிலும் !?

units.claim_summary: Bhatta Somesvara’s explanation is used to argue that kadigai took its name from a pot-based examination method in which marked slips identified Vedic passages students had to recite.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பெயர் விளக்கம்?

units.claim_summary: The Sanskrit passage describing the kadigai examination is parsed to show that marked portions of Vedic text were placed in a pot and drawn as a test of mastery.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சிறிது ஸம்ஸ்க்ருத பாடம்?

units.claim_summary: The use of a pot in Vedic examination is interpreted symbolically as fitting a tradition in which the vessel contains and distributes the knowledge that sustains the larger tree of dharma.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கும்பத்தின் பொருத்தம்?

units.claim_summary: Tamil inscriptional evidence is surveyed to show that major Vedic colleges existed outside the famous kadigais, with organized curricula, teachers, students, endowments, and rules protecting full-time study.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தமிழகத்தின் வேதக் கலாசாலைகள்?

units.claim_summary: The presence of Atharva Veda students in an eleventh-century Tamil school is cited as evidence that a branch later regarded as weak in living practice still had institutional study at that time.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அதர்வ வேதமும் அநுஷ்டானத்தில்?

units.claim_summary: Educational endowments are shown supporting grammar, Mimamsa, Vedanta, and other disciplines alongside Vedic study, demonstrating a broader scholastic curriculum than scripture recitation alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பல சாஸ்த்ரங்களுக்கு ஆதரவு?

units.claim_summary: Inscriptional distinctions between Vedic Brahmins and specialists in Pancharatra, Vaikhanasa, and Shaiva Agamas are used to show that Vedic and Agamic learning were related but institutionally distinguishable streams.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேத – ஆகமங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The coexistence of Vedic and Agamic study under common institutional patronage is presented as an example of unity that does not erase differences among religious disciplines.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸமரச அம்சம்?

units.claim_summary: Temples are described as major educational sites in later periods, with dedicated teaching spaces supporting grammar and secular as well as religious learning rather than functioning only as ritual centers.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆலயமும் வித்யையும்?

units.claim_summary: The achievements of older educational and artistic institutions are contrasted with modern decline, and the comparison is used to urge recovery without pretending that every old numerical claim is literal.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பெருமையும் சிறுமையும்?

units.claim_summary: Public support for indigenous learning is urged, but state control is treated cautiously because preservation is said to require fidelity to the disciplines’ own methods rather than administrative modernization alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்வதேச வித்யைகளுக்கு “திட்டம்”?

units.claim_summary: Revived traditional schools should preserve the disciplines’ characteristic residential, concentrated, and morally regulated modes of study as far as present circumstances allow, instead of copying ordinary urban schools.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அதற்குரிய முறைப்படி?

units.claim_summary: Ordinary village statistical boards prompt the proposal that public life should measure moral and civic quality rather than only population and material facts.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கிராமப் புள்ளிவிவரங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Because moral worth cannot be reduced to a simple list, crime and litigation statistics are proposed as an imperfect but observable indicator for comparing social conduct.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேவைப்படும் ஒரு புள்ளிவிவரம்?

units.claim_summary: Modern schooling is criticized for increasing technical cleverness without necessarily improving character, with crime and corruption offered as attributed social observations rather than established causal science.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about படிப்பும் குற்றமும்?

units.claim_summary: The apparent contradiction between praising education and observing misconduct among educated people is resolved by arguing that knowledge without devotion, restraint, and moral formation can strengthen ego rather than virtue.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முரண்பாடு எதனால்??

units.claim_summary: Religious instruction in Western Christian and Muslim settings is discussed comparatively to argue that nominal religious content is insufficient unless discipline and lived observance shape conduct; the comparison remains attributed.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வெள்ளையர் நாடுகளும் இஸ்லாமியர் நாடுகளும்?

units.claim_summary: Communist societies are used as a political-social comparison: external law may restrain conduct, but the discourse prefers internalized divine and scriptural accountability to fear of human punishment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கம்யூனிஸ்ட் நாடுகளில்?

units.claim_summary: Learning becomes beneficial only when joined to humility, devotion, religious discipline, and reverence for the teacher, because education that inflates ego is presented as morally dangerous.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விநயத்தோடு இணைந்த வித்யை?

units.claim_summary: Residential gurukula life is valued above abstract exhortation because daily service to a visible teacher is said to provide a practical discipline for reducing ego.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அஹம் அடிபடவே குருகுலம்?

units.claim_summary: The claim that gurukula education is impossible today is rejected by pointing to arts and crafts still transmitted through apprenticeship, so partial revival is presented as practical rather than nostalgic fantasy.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஏன் சாத்யமில்லை??

units.claim_summary: The public is assigned responsibility for reviving at least limited gurukula-style learning, especially Vedic education, by sustaining teachers who cannot support such transmission alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பொதுமக்களின் பொறுப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Vedic preservation is said to require coordinated and durable support for both teachers and students, including adequate maintenance and incentives without turning the tradition into a luxury profession.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேதவித்யை வளர?

units.claim_summary: Learning pursued for its own sake is ranked above learning pursued for money, while financial support is accepted as a practical secondary arrangement when pure noncommercial transmission cannot be sustained.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வித்யையும் வித்தமும்?

units.claim_summary: Bhikshacharya is presented as the most renunciatory educational model because both teacher and student organize life around transmission and study rather than income or comfort.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிக்ஷாசா்யம்?

units.claim_summary: A rotating household-meal system is proposed as a practicable adaptation of student alms, distributing support across families while preserving some dependence on community rather than salary.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வாரச் சாப்பாடு?

units.claim_summary: The austerity of self-sacrificing teachers and students should be met by public generosity, yet support should be structured so that it does not destroy the very spirit of simplicity it intends to preserve.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவர்கள் தியாகமும் நமது தியாகமும்?

units.claim_summary: Traditional learning should ultimately lead toward Brahma-vidya while also restoring Vedic commentary, Vedangas, astronomy, mathematics, and Vedanta; modern comparative research is welcomed only if it does not casually dismiss inherited disciplines.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேத பாஷ்யம், வேதாங்கம், வேதாந்தம்?

units.claim_summary: Comparative study of philosophical systems is encouraged so that Indian and non-Indian traditions can be understood in relation to one another rather than studied in isolated intellectual compartments.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பல ஸித்தாந்த ஒப்புவுமை?

units.claim_summary: Puranic learning is said to survive partly through public discourse, but deeper study of the full Purana corpus and other Vedic ancillary disciplines still requires organized preservation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about புராணம்?

units.claim_summary: Mantra and Agama traditions are presented as large bodies of technical religious knowledge governing consecration, temple construction, worship, and ritual presence, and therefore needing serious transmission.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆகம சாஸ்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: Vastu is presented as a traditional discipline extending from temple siting to settlement and house design, and its textual tradition is urged to be studied rather than reduced to isolated popular rules.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வாஸ்து சாஸ்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: Sculptural knowledge is treated as a disciplined sacred art whose theory and hereditary practice should be preserved together; claims about caste-based transmission are historical-social and require context.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சில்ப சாஸ்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: Local hereditary arts, including performance and ritual crafts, are treated as knowledge traditions worth sustaining before they disappear with the last living practitioners.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கிராமக் கலைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Revival requires creating teachers as well as students: researchers should recover old texts and methods, master them critically, and then establish new lines of instruction.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசிரியர்களையும் உண்டாக்க வேண்டும்?

units.claim_summary: Disciplines such as nadi and other traditions said to exceed presently known natural laws should be investigated rather than dismissed solely as superstition, but such claims require external scientific verification and are not certified by attestation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இயற்கை விதிகளுக்குப் பிடிபடாத வித்யைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Ayurveda, Siddha, and regional medicine should not be left only to scattered practitioners; their textual and practical traditions require deliberate study and transmission, without implying modern medical validation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வைத்ய சாஸ்திரம்?

units.claim_summary: Potentially hazardous or easily abused disciplines such as alchemy should be taught primarily as theory unless competent practical mastery exists, because unsupervised practice can encourage fraud and harm.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘தியரி’ மட்டும், ப்ராக்டிஸ்’ இல்லை?

units.claim_summary: Vedanta, like yoga, cannot be reduced to book study or assigned a realized teacher on demand; serious transmission requires qualified teachers, appropriate students, and continuity of practice.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேதாந்த விஷயத்திலும் இப்படியே?

units.claim_summary: The immediate preservation task is to identify remaining traditional scholars, place them in viable teaching settings, record endangered knowledge, and create students before living transmission disappears.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about செய்யவேண்டிய பணிகள்?

units.claim_summary: A person who has genuinely mastered a discipline is said to incur a duty to teach it, completing learning through study, understanding, practice, and transmission rather than keeping knowledge private.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கற்றவன் கற்பிப்பவனாக வேண்டும்?

units.claim_summary: Traditional scholars need both material maintenance and public honor so that rare learning becomes socially viable and teachers are encouraged to form successor lineages.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திரவிய உதவியும் ஸமூஹ கௌரவமும்?

units.claim_summary: Preservation is not only about sponsoring a few specialists; ordinary people are urged to become serious students in at least one field suited to their aptitude so learned culture remains socially broad.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஒவ்வொருவரும் வித்வானாக வேண்டும்?

units.claim_summary: Any art, science, or scholarship should be linked to the divine and offered as service, because dedicating knowledge to a higher end is presented as a way to reduce intellectual ego.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அஹம் குறைய “அவனை”த் தொடர்புறுத்துக!?

units.claim_summary: Time otherwise spent in distraction can be redirected to disciplined learning, which is presented both as wholesome recreation and as a way of developing capacities distinctive to human life.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வீணாகும் நேரம் வித்யைக்கு ஆகட்டும்?

units.claim_summary: Older references to communities of learned people are used to argue that broad scholarly culture once extended beyond a tiny professional class and should again become a social aspiration.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அனைவரும் வித்வானாயிருந்த காலம்?

units.claim_summary: Age and an already established way of life are not treated as absolute barriers to serious study; late learners are urged to test that assumption through disciplined effort.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வாழ்க்கை முறையும் வயதும் தடையாகா?

units.claim_summary: Because modern government is not expected to preserve every traditional discipline, responsibility is placed chiefly on the public and on disciples connected with teaching institutions and guru lineages.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அரசாங்கமல்ல; மக்களும் சீடர்களுமே பொறுப்பு?

units.claim_summary: A culture that rewards shallow knowledge while neglecting deep scholarship risks losing entire disciplines, so genuine scholars must be recognized and supported before their transmission ends.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அரைகுறை ஞானத்துக்கே ஆதரவு?

units.claim_summary: Personal encounters with self-effacing scholars are used as examples of learning pursued without hunger for wealth or fame, illustrating the ideal of scholarship sustained by dedication rather than recognition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நேரில் கண்ட ஆதர்ச வித்வான்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The scholar’s renunciation of money and fame does not excuse society from support; precisely because such scholars do not market themselves, communities should protect their work for future generations.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வருங்காலத்துக்காக?

units.claim_summary: Ancient disciplines survive only if knowledge remains joined to living practice and apprenticeship; academic papers, books, and conferences alone cannot replace embodied transmission.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உயிரோடு ஒட்டிவைக்க வேண்டும்?

units.claim_summary: Gurukula or at least residential study under disciplined teachers is proposed across many fields because close formation is said to transmit both knowledge and character better than detached classroom instruction.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எல்லாத் துறையிலும் குருகுல வாஸம்?

units.claim_summary: The long appeal for educational revival ends in prayer that the Goddess as the embodiment of knowledge grant the insight and grace needed to restore traditional learning.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அம்பாள் அருள்வாளாக!?

units.claim_summary: Vedic and early textual references to assemblies are interpreted as evidence that consultative and participatory elements existed in ancient governance, while the historical inference remains source-dependent rather than a claim that modern democracy existed unchanged.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேதத்திலும் ஜனநாயக அம்சம்*?

units.claim_summary: Occupational and social groups are described as having forms of self-government within a larger polity, an attributed historical account that also reflects a caste-organized social order requiring context.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜாதி நாட்டாண்மை?

units.claim_summary: Public administration is said to require competence, so direct rule by everyone is rejected in favor of selecting people with demonstrated qualifications for complex governing responsibilities.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தகுதி தேவை?

units.claim_summary: A king is presented as a unifying national head whose authority is constrained by dharma, law, ministers, and advisers rather than conceived as unrestricted personal rule.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேசத் தலைமைக்கு அரசன்?

units.claim_summary: Local administration is distinguished from kingship: village affairs are entrusted to a representative council with a functional head rather than to a hereditary miniature king.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஊர்த் தலைமை?

units.claim_summary: Village council members are described as entering office through a local selection process rather than royal appointment, giving residents an institutional share in administration without equating the system with universal suffrage.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேர்தல் மூலம் ஊர் ஸபையில் அங்கம்?

units.claim_summary: Modern republican representation is compared with older forms of limited local participation, emphasizing that even a republic must delegate governing work to a smaller number of representatives.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குடியரசு, ஜனநாயகம்?

units.claim_summary: Universal adult voting is questioned from the standpoint that judging a candidate also requires civic knowledge and responsibility; this is an attributed political argument, not a neutral factual conclusion.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அபிப்ராய பேதம்?

units.claim_summary: The old village system is introduced as unusual because it avoids both royal appointment and ordinary vote-counting, preparing the case for the kudavolai selection method.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விசித்ர அம்சம் கொண்ட தேர்தல் முறை?

units.claim_summary: Chola dynastic history is reviewed to place the Uttiramerur election inscriptions within a longer Tamil political chronology; the dating and genealogy are historical claims requiring external verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சோழ வம்சம்?

units.claim_summary: Parantaka-period inscriptions are identified as evidence for a tenth-century village-level selection system, with the scope explicitly distinguished from elections to a whole kingdom or modern legislature.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேர்தல் குறித்த கல்வெட்டு?

units.claim_summary: The village assembly is described as being organized through territorial units or families that supplied candidates to the larger council.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about க்ராம ஸபையின் அமைப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Multiple inscriptions, especially the two Uttiramerur records, are treated as documentary evidence for local-government rules and their revision, while royal oversight is acknowledged alongside local autonomy.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கல்வெட்டைப் பற்றிய விவரம்?

units.claim_summary: Officials named in the inscription show Brahmin and Vellala participation in administration, which is used to complicate a simplistic claim that office belonged exclusively to one varna; the caste categories remain historical context.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அந்தண – வேளாள அதிகாரிகள்?

units.claim_summary: Uttiramerur candidate qualifications include property, residence, age, learning, and conduct, and the later inscription’s revisions are used to show that administrative rules could be amended.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேட்பாளரின் யோக்யாதாம்சங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Practical administrative rules may be revised as circumstances change, but the discourse distinguishes such amendments from what it regards as foundational dharmic principles that should not be altered for convenience.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருத்தக் கூடிய விதிகளும் – திருத்தக் கூடாத விதிகளும்?

units.claim_summary: Public officials are expected to combine scriptural or intellectual knowledge with practical competence, because scholarship without administrative ability is presented as insufficient for governance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சாஸ்திர அறிவும், காரியத்திறனும்?

units.claim_summary: Material integrity and moral purity are treated as the core qualifications for public office, with property rules interpreted primarily as safeguards against corruption rather than as status alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜீவஸாரமான தகுதி : அர்த்த சுத்தமும் ஆத்ம சுத்தமும்?

units.claim_summary: Term limits prevent continuous occupation of village office and are explained as a safeguard against entrenched power and the moral risks of prolonged authority.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தொடர்ந்து அங்கம் வகிக்கலாகாது?

units.claim_summary: Restrictions on close relatives of recent officeholders are interpreted as another anti-entrenchment rule intended to prevent public administration from becoming family control.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உறவினர் உதவாது?

units.claim_summary: Muslim and British periods are compared as regimes that altered indigenous institutions and religious life in different ways; the discussion includes contested historical and interreligious claims that require attribution and external verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about துருக்கர், வெள்ளையர் ஆட்சிகளில்?

units.claim_summary: Post-independence secular government is criticized for intervening in Hindu custom while allowing other religious communities more autonomy; this is a contested political-religious claim presented as the discourse’s view, not established here as neutral fact.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘ஸொந்த’ ஸர்க்காரின் அத்துமீறல்!?

units.claim_summary: A property qualification is defended against the charge of vested interest by arguing that some tangible stake or deposit can signal seriousness and responsibility, though the policy judgment is explicitly normative.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸொத்துத் தகுதி பற்றி?

units.claim_summary: Independent means are argued to reduce susceptibility to bribery, an attributed social claim that is compared with modern security requirements rather than treated as a demonstrated causal law.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குறைவான லஞ்ச ஹேது?

units.claim_summary: The old rule against accepting bribes is connected with property and security qualifications, which are defended as attempts to reduce temptation and protect public assets.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கையூட்டு?

units.claim_summary: Experience managing one’s own property is offered as preparation for stewarding common property, because public administration requires accounting, conservation, and responsible expenditure.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸொத்துப் பரிபாலன அநுபவம் அவசியம்?

units.claim_summary: The requirement that an officeholder live in a house on his own site is interpreted as evidence of rootedness and long-term stake in the village whose resources he will manage.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “தன் மனை” என்றதன் காரணம்?

units.claim_summary: Both minimum and maximum age limits are defended as balancing maturity and experience against the decline or rigidity that may accompany advanced age; the political judgment is contextual rather than universal.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வயதுத் தகுதி?

units.claim_summary: Truthfulness is presented as the indispensable moral foundation of dharmic public administration, because rules cannot protect a polity when officials themselves abandon honesty.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தர்ம ஒழுங்கின் ஸத்ய அடிப்படை?

units.claim_summary: Age rules can admit exceptional elders when demonstrable capacity remains, showing that qualification is treated as a practical safeguard rather than an inflexible numerical fetish.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விதிவிலக்கான வயோதிகர்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Public service is distinguished from ordinary salaried office: representatives are expected to devote limited periods to common work rather than convert civic responsibility into permanent employment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அலுவலக வேலையும் பொதுச்சபை பணியும்?

units.claim_summary: Experienced elders may serve as an advisory body without monopolizing executive office, preserving institutional memory while leaving active administration open to renewal.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மூதறிஞர்களின் ஆலோசனைக் குழு?

units.claim_summary: Rotation rules are praised for preventing individuals or factions from converting temporary responsibility into permanent political dominance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆதிக்கத்தை நிரந்தரமாக்கிக் கொள்ளாதிருக்க?

units.claim_summary: A defined level of learning is required for village office because representatives must understand law, records, and public duties rather than rely only on popularity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கல்வித் தகுதி?

units.claim_summary: Although inscriptional language often reflects Brahmin settlements, the principles of qualification and public duty are argued not to be inherently limited to Brahmins; the historical social setting nevertheless requires caste context.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ராமணரை மட்டும் குறிப்பதாகாது?

units.claim_summary: Administrative rules are interpreted as aiming at the living health of the community rather than formal compliance alone, so qualifications must be judged by whether they protect effective public life.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உயிர் நிலை?

units.claim_summary: Collective corruption is traced to failures of personal integrity among officials and citizens, making moral self-discipline rather than institutional design alone the proposed remedy.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸர்வஜன அசுத்திக்கு ஹேது?

units.claim_summary: Purity of motive and conduct is presented as the decisive qualification underlying all external rules for public service.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்ம சுத்தம்?

units.claim_summary: Rules barring immediate re-election and close relatives are interpreted as safeguards intended to prevent corruption from reappearing after an otherwise qualified person enters office.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிற்பாடும் அசுத்தி ஏற்படாதிருக்க?

units.claim_summary: Mandatory rotation after a short term is praised for bringing new people into administration and preventing a closed circle from monopolizing civic responsibility.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about புது ரத்தம் பிடிக்க?

units.claim_summary: Excluding close relatives of previous officeholders is treated as a backbone of ethical administration because successors might otherwise conceal or continue a relative’s misconduct.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தார்மிக நிர்வாஹத்தின் முதுகெலும்பு?

units.claim_summary: Hereditary continuity is defended only for the symbolic national kingship described here, while local councils are said to require rotation and anti-nepotism rules; the comparison is a normative political argument.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ராஜபீட விஷயமும் ஊர்ச்சபை விஷயமும்?

units.claim_summary: Misconduct while in office is said to justify immediate removal and permanent future disqualification rather than merely a temporary pause before returning to power.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பதவிநீக்கமும் நிரந்தரத் தடையும்?

units.claim_summary: The inscription’s extension of disqualification to specified relatives is presented as evidence of how aggressively the system tried to block family networks from preserving corrupt influence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தகுதி இழக்கும் உறவினர்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The traditional list of grave sins and violent offenses is used as a moral disqualification for public office; the religious-legal categories are historical and include violence that requires context.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பஞ்சமாபாதகம்?

units.claim_summary: Older governance is portrayed as aligning religious notions of sin with civil notions of crime, while the present separation of scriptural norm and secular law is contrasted with that model.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சாஸ்த்ரமும் சட்டமும்?

units.claim_summary: Public humiliation, forgery, and related offenses are cited as older grounds for civic disqualification; punitive customs described in the source are historical material rather than endorsement for modern practice.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தகுதித் தடைகள் சில?

units.claim_summary: The kudavolai system is emphasized as neither candidate-driven campaigning nor ordinary voter balloting: qualified names entered a selection process without applicants soliciting votes.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேட்பாளர் இல்லாத-வாக்காளர் இல்லாத தேர்தல்?

units.claim_summary: Potential representatives were first identified from each local unit among people already regarded as qualified, making communal screening precede the random or lot-like final selection.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அபேக்ஷகர் யார்??

units.claim_summary: Selection and election were entrusted to bodies distinct from the outgoing officeholders, an arrangement interpreted as reducing incumbents’ ability to manipulate their successors.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸெலக்ஷன், எலெக்ஷன் பொறுப்பாளர்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The kudavolai procedure is described as placing qualified names in pots and having an uninvolved child draw the final name, symbolically removing factional bargaining from the last step.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேர்தல் நடந்த விதம்?

units.claim_summary: Public reading and verification of the drawn palm leaf are presented as transparency safeguards designed to leave little room for secret substitution or manipulation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஒளிவு மறைவுக்கு இடமில்லை?

units.claim_summary: Because candidates did not campaign for personal popularity, the old procedure is praised as selecting from pre-qualified people without making charisma or party image the decisive factor.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தனிமனிதக் கவர்ச்சி அம்சமே இல்லை?

units.claim_summary: The system did not choose by numerical majority; it first narrowed the field to qualified people and then used selection by lot, which the discourse contrasts with factional majority politics.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பெரும்பான்மை அடிப்படை இல்லை?

units.claim_summary: The inscription’s aspiration that the arrangement continue as long as sun and moon endure is read as evidence of confidence in the system, even though the institution itself did not remain permanent.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘சந்திர ஸூரியர் உள்ளவரை’?

units.claim_summary: Village administration is described as divided among specialized committees responsible for annual oversight, gardens, tanks, revenue, gold, and other functions, with members assigned according to experience and capacity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நிர்வாஹப் பிரிவுகள்?

units.claim_summary: The old election story is revisited because its principles—qualification, rotation, transparency, and reduced faction—are proposed as material from which modern democratic practice might learn.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about புதுக்கதையும் பழங்கதையும்?

units.claim_summary: Modern electoral politics is criticized for money, propaganda, fragmented vote shares, weak discipline, and party incentives; these are political judgments of the discourse rather than neutral empirical conclusions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கவலைக்குரிய அம்சங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Political responsibility should follow civic maturation rather than precede it, and local elections are urged to be insulated from party competition until voters and institutions are better prepared; this remains a normative political prescription.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பக்குவம் செய்தபின் பொறுப்புத் தருக !?

units.claim_summary: The old system offers reassurance because it foregrounded moral and financial qualification and minimized campaign personality, patronage, and factional inducement.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பழைய தேர்தல் தரும் தேறுதல்?

units.claim_summary: The apparent weakness of random selection among several qualified people is answered by arguing that local scale, prior screening, short terms, and anti-corruption safeguards mattered more than ranking popularity; the system is not proposed for literal unmodified adoption.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குறையும், குறைக்கு ஸமாதானமும்?

units.claim_summary: Rama-rajya is invoked as an ideal of rule grounded in the ruler’s dharma and the subjects’ moral order, not merely in administrative efficiency or popular preference.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ராமராஜ்யம்?

units.claim_summary: Deva and asura are interpreted primarily as moral-spiritual tendencies rather than biological species, distinguishing conduct oriented toward truth from conduct driven by ego and desire.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேவாஸுரர் யார்??

units.claim_summary: Asuric behavior is said to arise when the mind turns away from its divine ground and makes desire, pride, and separateness its governing principles.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அஸுரப்போக்கு தோன்றுவது ஏன்??

units.claim_summary: Fear is traced to duality because perceiving another as separate creates the possibility of loss, threat, and conflict.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பயத்துக்கு இடம் தரும் த்வைதம்?

units.claim_summary: Advaita is presented as complete fearlessness because no second independent reality remains from which danger could arise.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அத்வைதமே அபயம்?

units.claim_summary: Liberation is identified with fearlessness in nondual awareness, while samsara is characterized by the insecurity produced through dualistic identification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அபயம் – மோக்ஷம் ; பயம் – ஸம்ஸாரம்?

units.claim_summary: Fear of hell may restrain harmful conduct at an early moral stage, but it is not treated as the final spiritual motive, which must mature toward knowledge and love.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நரக பயம்?

units.claim_summary: The mind is presented as the immediate cause of bondage because identification with its thoughts, desires, and distinctions makes the Self appear limited.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனமே பந்த காரணம்?

units.claim_summary: The Self is described as intrinsically blissful and free of mental agitation, so true happiness is not produced by thought but uncovered when mental disturbance subsides.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனமற்ற ஆத்மாவின் ஆனந்தம்?

units.claim_summary: Deep sleep is used to argue that a basic sense of existence persists even when ordinary mental activity is absent, suggesting that personal reality is not identical with thought.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனமற்ற நிலையிலும் “நாம்”?

units.claim_summary: The real “I” is identified with the enduring Self rather than the changing body, roles, memories, or mental states ordinarily taken to define the person.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நிஜ `நாம்’?

units.claim_summary: Bare awareness of existence without the usual admixture of thought is presented as a pointer toward the Self that underlies mental personality.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனக் கலப்பில்லாத உயிர் உணர்வு?

units.claim_summary: Ordinary life mistakes experiences occurring in mind for the life of the Self; practice is directed toward recognizing the witnessing reality rather than its mental coverings.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்ம உணர்வும், மனோ வாழ்க்கையும்?

units.claim_summary: Mind appears as a second thing over against the Self and is therefore treated as the first emergence of duality, from which the many objects and fears of experience follow.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்மாவுக்கு த்விதீயமான மனம்?

units.claim_summary: Liberation and fearlessness are said to consist in freedom from mind’s binding identification and abidance as the nondual Self.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்மாநுபவமே அபய மோக்ஷம்?

units.claim_summary: Dharma is compared to a tighter therapeutic binding used to loosen the older knots of impulsive karma: disciplined action is initially restrictive but preparatory to freedom.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கர்மத்தளை தளர்த்தும் தர்மம்?

units.claim_summary: The Upanishadic distinction between preyas and shreyas teaches that what is immediately pleasant may differ from what is truly beneficial, so spiritual discipline chooses long-term good over immediate preference.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரேயஸ், ச்ரேயஸ்?

units.claim_summary: Dharmic action is described as medicine for karmic disorder: repeated disciplined conduct gradually retrains the mind even when the practice initially feels unpleasant.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கர்ம நோய்க்கு தர்ம மருந்து?

units.claim_summary: Nishkamya karma is not itself the direct cause of liberation, because action still operates through mind; its function is to purify the mind so knowledge can arise.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தார்மிக கர்மா நேரான மோக்ஷ உபாயமல்ல?

units.claim_summary: Love and devotion are introduced as the highest constructive mental tendencies, capable of replacing harmful thought-patterns and concentrating the mind on God and living beings.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அன்பு, பக்தி?

units.claim_summary: Scripturally prescribed action is not merely external behavior, because the intention and sacred recollection accompanying action shape the mind and its future tendencies.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சாஸ்த்ர கர்மாவுக்குப் பின்னணியான ஸத்சிந்தனை?

units.claim_summary: Action and meditation are complementary for the beginner: selfless sacred work steadies and purifies the mind, while limited meditation trains it toward sustained inwardness.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கார்யமும் த்யானமும்?

units.claim_summary: Karma-yoga is defined by action without possessive attachment to its fruits, using work to weaken karmic impressions while retaining the higher desire for Self-realization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கர்மயோகமும் பற்றின்மையும்?

units.claim_summary: Good action may not yield visible welfare immediately because individual and collective past karma are invoked as additional causes; the claim is theological rather than empirically verifiable causation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸத்கர்மா பலிக்காததேன்??

units.claim_summary: Karma and devotion cannot themselves eliminate all duality, but by purifying and concentrating the mind they reduce occasions for fear and prepare the movement toward nondual realization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பய வாய்ப்புக் குறைதல்?

units.claim_summary: The cosmos is compared to a divine drama in which creation continues through recurring cycles and dissolutions; pralaya is distinguished from final liberation because temporary absorption is not identity with Brahman.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உலக நாடகமும் ப்ரளயங்களும்?

units.claim_summary: Since the whole world will not collectively abandon samsara, spiritual aspirants should use their own duties to promote both inner purification and the highest attainable welfare of ordinary social life.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உலக வாழ்வின் உயர் நலன்களுக்காக?

units.claim_summary: Following another person’s dharma is discouraged because discipline must grow from one’s own nature, responsibilities, and stage of development rather than imitation that destabilizes the mind.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பரதர்மம் ஏன் கூடாது??

units.claim_summary: The force that pushes a person toward wrongdoing even against better judgment is identified as desire, which becomes anger and compulsion when obstructed.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாபத்தில் தள்ளும் சக்தி எது??

units.claim_summary: Desire and anger are presented as linked forms of the same rajasic force: desire seeks possession, and frustrated desire transforms into hostility.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காம – க்ரோதம்?

units.claim_summary: A wide range of harmful tendencies is traced back to desire, making regulation of craving the central practical target rather than treating each vice as wholly separate.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தீயவை அனைத்தும் ஆசையிலிருந்தே?

units.claim_summary: Even experiences initially called happiness become sources of suffering when the mind clings to them, because pleasure creates dependence, fear of loss, and renewed craving.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸந்தோஷத்தினாலேயே கஷ்டம்?

units.claim_summary: True happiness is distinguished from temporary satisfaction: satisfaction ends a particular want for a moment, while enduring bliss is said to belong to the Self that lacks nothing.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆனந்தமும் த்ருப்தியும்?

units.claim_summary: Human beings can be ruined through attachment to any one of the five senses, so the combined pull of all five requires disciplined restraint rather than confidence in mere intelligence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஐம்புலனாலும் அழிவடையும் மானுடன்?

units.claim_summary: Lasting happiness cannot be produced by desire because every desired object is limited, changing, and dependent on circumstances.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சாச்வத இன்பம் ஆசையால் விளையாது?

units.claim_summary: Pleasure arising from objects changes with time, place, condition, and mental state, showing that the object itself cannot contain a fixed quantity of happiness.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கால – தேசாதிகளின் பாதிப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Even the same body desires different things at different ages and conditions, demonstrating that craving is constructed by changing mind-body circumstances rather than by permanent need.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தன் உடம்பிலேயே ஆசை வித்யாஸம்?

units.claim_summary: Mind stands between the Self and the senses, interpreting sensory contact and converting it into attraction, aversion, memory, and personal experience.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனம் ஆத்மாவுக்கும் புலனுக்கும் இடைப்பட்டது?

units.claim_summary: Mental pleasures are also unstable because thought, imagination, status, and intellectual achievement change and therefore cannot provide permanent fulfillment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனத்தின் இன்பமும் நிலைத்ததல்ல?

units.claim_summary: Every state short of nondual realization retains some dependence on another object or condition and therefore some vulnerability to disappointment and suffering.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அத்வைதம் தவிர அனைத்திலும் துக்கம்?

units.claim_summary: Desire can lead a person to harm others for private satisfaction, showing why unchecked craving is both an individual and social moral danger.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிறரை வருத்தியும்?

units.claim_summary: Attachment obstructs generosity, truthfulness, restraint, and other higher qualities because the mind begins evaluating conduct by whether it serves its desired object.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உயர் பண்புகளுக்கு ஊறு செய்யும் ஆசை?

units.claim_summary: The finite mind cannot contain unbroken infinite bliss, so the quest for complete happiness must culminate beyond mental experience in the Self.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அகண்ட ஆனந்தம் மனத்துக்கு இல்லை?

units.claim_summary: Outer conflict will recur as long as craving and possessiveness remain, so lasting peace is said to require attacking desire at its psychological root rather than only negotiating its external consequences.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about யுத்தம் தீர ஆசையை அழிக்க!?

units.claim_summary: Death—and specifically self-inflicted death—is rejected as a way to end desire or suffering; within the karmic framework presented here, unresolved tendencies and consequences are said to continue beyond bodily death.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மரணத்தால் ஆசை அழியுமா??

units.claim_summary: Repeated birth is described as the consequence of desires and actions that keep the individual tied to unfinished experience, making samsara itself the penalty of craving.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிறவித் தண்டனை?

units.claim_summary: Like acquiring a taste for an initially bitter fruit, repeated indulgence can make harmful desire seem sweet, showing how habit reverses moral judgment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேப்பம்பழத் தித்திப்பு?
