units.claim_summary: Persistent effort is required because desires have been strengthened over long habit and cannot be removed by a single insight or occasional act of restraint.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விடாமுயற்சி வேண்டும்?

units.claim_summary: Desire operates through the mind but rests on the deeper existence-consciousness supplied by the Self, so its activity depends on a ground it does not understand.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசையின் செயலும் ‘அதிஷ்டான’மும்?

units.claim_summary: Arjuna’s difficulty illustrates the universal problem of a mind that knows what is right yet is pulled by entrenched tendencies, making disciplined practice necessary alongside instruction.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அர்ஜுனனின் குறை?

units.claim_summary: Krishna’s remedy is summarized as repeated practice and dispassion: the wandering mind is brought back again and again while attachment to its objects is deliberately weakened.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கண்ணன் சொல்லும் உபாயம்?

units.claim_summary: The Self is described as changeless through all alterations of body, senses, and mind, providing the stable reality against which change is recognized.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்மா: மாறுபாடு அற்றது?

units.claim_summary: The true Self is contrasted with the mind’s assumed personality, which is treated as a temporary costume mistakenly claimed as the real person.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘நிஜ’ ஆத்மாவும் பொய் வேஷ மனஸும்?

units.claim_summary: Mind and senses function only because consciousness illumines them; the Self is therefore presented as their enabling ground without itself becoming an agent of their changing activities.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்மாவினாலேயே மனத்தின் இயக்கம்?

units.claim_summary: The Self simply is, whereas the mind is defined by doing and modification; spiritual practice moves from compulsive activity toward recognition of the underlying state of being.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இருக்கும் நிலையும், செய்யும் நிலையும்?

units.claim_summary: Desire is likened to hunger that grows through feeding, because repeated satisfaction often strengthens rather than exhausts the habit of wanting.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசைப் பசியின் விளைவுகள்?

units.claim_summary: Attraction and rejection are two sides of the same binding relation to objects, so liberation requires freedom from compulsive taking as well as compulsive avoidance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கொள்ளுவதும் தள்ளுவதும்?

units.claim_summary: The absence of thought in sleep is not liberation because ignorance remains; the goal is conscious freedom from mental bondage, not unconscious blankness.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தூக்கமல்ல வழி?

units.claim_summary: Dispassion removes fuel from desire while repeated practice steadies attention, making vairagya and abhyasa mutually necessary for mastery of mind.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வைராக்யமும் அப்யாஸமும்?

units.claim_summary: The Self is characterized as bliss, knowledge, and peace, and these are presented not as qualities acquired by practice but as what becomes evident when obscuring mental activity quiets.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆனந்த ஞான சாந்தம்?

units.claim_summary: Object-derived pleasure is described as a reflected ray of the Self’s own bliss, temporarily revealed when desire subsides after obtaining an object.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்மாநந்த கிரணமே வெளியின்பம்?

units.claim_summary: The peace-bliss of the Self cannot be fully conceptualized by mind because mind knows through distinctions, whereas the claimed reality is beyond subject-object division.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனத்துக்குப் புரியாத சாந்தாநந்தம்?

units.claim_summary: Deep sleep is used as an analogy for mind’s temporary subsidence and experienced rest, while its unconsciousness prevents it from being equated with realization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நித்ரை நிலை?

units.claim_summary: Dream shows the mind constructing an experienced world from its own impressions, supporting the argument that waking experience too is mediated by mental projection.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கனவு நிலை?

units.claim_summary: Mind becomes subject to the Self through disciplined purification, inquiry, devotion, and repeated withdrawal from identification rather than through violent suppression.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனம் ஆத்மாவிடம் வசப்படுவது எப்படி??

units.claim_summary: Divine grace is presented as indispensable to the final mastery of mind, complementing personal effort rather than making practice unnecessary.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வர க்ருபையால்?

units.claim_summary: Living examples of realized or deeply disciplined persons are offered as experiential evidence that extraordinary peace and freedom from ordinary mental agitation are possible; biographical claims remain externally verifiable.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரத்யக்ஷச் சான்றுகள்?

units.claim_summary: Jivanmuktas are presented as persons liberated while embodied, whose continued bodily activity does not re-create inward bondage because identification with the doer has ended.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜீவன் முக்தர்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The liberated person is not merely someone who “has” knowledge as a possession but one in whom the distinction between knower and known has dissolved into the reality known.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘உடைய’ அல்ல, உடையவரே!?

units.claim_summary: Even desire for happiness is ultimately interpreted as an indirect desire for the Self, because every finite object is sought for the sense of completeness it seems to promise.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசையும் ஆத்மாவைக் குறித்ததே?

units.claim_summary: Mythic destruction of asuric forces is interpreted inwardly as victory over egoistic tendencies, turning the battle narrative into a metaphor for Self-mastery.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அஸுரப் படை அழிவு ஆத்ம ஜயமே?

units.claim_summary: The senses are not condemned absolutely; when disciplined and redirected, they can support worship, learning, and the gradual movement toward higher awareness.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இந்த்ரியத்துக்கும் உயர்வுண்டு?

units.claim_summary: The Self is identified with sat, pure being that does not come and go with particular experiences, bodies, or mental states.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘ஸத்’தான ஆத்மா?

units.claim_summary: Practice must proceed gradually from disciplined conduct and devotion through concentration and inquiry toward stable recognition of the Self rather than attempting to imitate the final state prematurely.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about படிப்படியாய் ஆத்ம நிலைக்கு?

units.claim_summary: The instruction to subdue the self by the self is explained by distinguishing the higher discriminating capacity aligned with the Self from the lower impulsive mind that must be trained.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘ஆத்மாவை ஆத்மாவினால் அடக்குவது’?

units.claim_summary: Ishvara functions as a bridge between dualistic devotion and nondual realization because the personal Lord can be worshipped as other while ultimately pointing to the same Brahman.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈசுவரன்: த்வைத – அத்வைதப் பாலம்?

units.claim_summary: Brahman, Atman, and Ishvara are distinguished conceptually according to standpoint—absolute reality, the Self, and the Lord associated with maya—without being treated as three independent ultimate realities in Advaita.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரஹ்மம் – ஆத்மா – ஈச்வரன்?

units.claim_summary: Final release from ignorance is attributed to Ishvara’s grace, which removes the obstacles that personal effort can prepare for but cannot by itself command.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விடுவிப்பு ஈசனாலேயே?

units.claim_summary: The empirical distinction between jiva and Ishvara is retained for devotion and practice even though Advaita ultimately denies that they are two independent realities.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜீவ – ஈச்வர வித்யாஸம்?

units.claim_summary: Intermediate spiritual stages are acknowledged so that instruction can move from ordinary dualistic experience through purification and devotion toward nondual knowledge without collapsing the path into the goal.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இடை நிலைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Teaching legitimately varies with the aspirant’s qualification, so apparently different scriptural instructions are reconciled as medicines suited to different levels rather than contradictions about one final truth.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அதிகாரிகளையொட்டி உபதேச மாறுபாடு?

units.claim_summary: Scripture remains necessary even when Ishvara is said to govern karma, because revealed teaching gives the embodied person a practical rule for aligning action and understanding with dharma.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈசன் செய்வதற்கு சாஸ்த்ரம் எதற்கு??

units.claim_summary: Shankara is cited to support the claim that knowledge itself is ultimately a divine gift, while study, discipline, and the guru prepare the mind to receive that illumination.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆதிசங்கரரும் கூறும் ஈசனது ஞானக் கொடை?

units.claim_summary: The dualistic relation to a guru is not an obstacle to Advaita because a provisional teacher-student distinction is precisely the means used to remove the disciple’s deeper ignorance of nonduality.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு என்ற த்வைதம் இடறுவதில்லை?

units.claim_summary: Maya, though responsible for appearance and ignorance, is also presented as the divine power through which scripture, guru, discrimination, and liberating knowledge become available.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மாயாசக்தியே ஞானமும் அளிப்பது?

units.claim_summary: The same Ishvara associated with karmic order is also presented as granting the knowledge that ends karmic bondage, so divine governance and liberation are not treated as competing functions.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கர்ம பந்தம் ஈசனால்; ஞான ஸித்தியும் அவனாலேயே!?

units.claim_summary: Discussion of Ishvara is deliberately suggestive rather than exhaustive because the personal Lord is a pedagogical standpoint within a teaching whose final subject is attributeless Brahman.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வரனைப் பற்றி ஸூசனை?

units.claim_summary: Knowledge of the Self destroys desire by removing the felt incompleteness from which craving arises, rather than by satisfying an endless series of objects.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்ம ஞானமே ஆசா நாசம்?

units.claim_summary: Liberation is presented as possible in embodied life, because freedom concerns the end of ignorance and identification rather than a destination reached only after physical death.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இகத்திலேயே மோக்ஷம்?

units.claim_summary: The ideal of liberation through knowledge is argued to predate Buddhism, countering the claim that Advaita merely borrowed its central goal from later Buddhist thought; the chronology is historical and requires external verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about புத்தருக்கு முற்பட்ட கருத்து?

units.claim_summary: When mind becomes still through knowledge, the Self is not newly created; what remains is the awareness that was present throughout mental activity but obscured by identification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனம் நின்றபின்?

units.claim_summary: True knowledge is identified specifically with knowledge of the Self, because information about objects cannot remove the fundamental mistake of taking the non-Self to be the Self.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மெய்யறிவு ஆத்ம ஞானமே?

units.claim_summary: Mental life is inherently incomplete because every thought divides experience into knower and known, leaving the mind dependent on change and unable to yield absolute fulfillment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மன வாழ்க்கையின் குறைபாடு?

units.claim_summary: Liberation does not require destroying the body but ending the mind’s false identification with body and experience as the whole of oneself.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about போகவேண்டியது தேஹமல்ல; மனமே?

units.claim_summary: Different traditions give different accounts of rebirth and liberation, but the discourse locates Advaita’s distinctive claim in ending ignorance rather than merely obtaining a better post-mortem state.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிறவி, முக்தி குறித்த கொள்கைகள்?

units.claim_summary: Because bondage is experienced now, effort toward freedom is necessary now rather than postponing spiritual practice to another world, life, or imagined future condition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேவை விடுதலைக்கு முயற்சியே!?

units.claim_summary: Samsara is finite in the sense that ignorance can end, and diverse Indian traditions are said to converge on the need for some form of release even when they explain it differently.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முடிவுள்ளதே ஸம்ஸாரம் ; ஏகோபித்த கருத்து?

units.claim_summary: Advaita accepts dualistic devotional and ethical stages as valid within practice while insisting that they are not the final account of reality; the path therefore includes rather than simply mocks lower standpoints.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about த்வைத நிலைகளை ஒப்புக்கொள்ளும் அத்வைதம்?

units.claim_summary: Unconditioned truth and happiness are located in nonduality because dependence on any second thing makes both knowledge and pleasure vulnerable to change.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸத்ய, ஸந்தோஷங்கள் அத்வைதத்திலேயே?

units.claim_summary: Fear is counted among the harms generated by desire because attachment immediately creates anxiety about obtaining, preserving, or losing the desired object.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆசையின் அனர்த்தங்களில் பயமும் ஒன்று?

units.claim_summary: Duality is the field of multiplicity in which mind compares, prefers, fears, and competes, so the spiritual problem is broader than any one pair of opposites.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பலவற்றைக் குறிக்கும் த்வைதம்?

units.claim_summary: Mind never exists as an isolated independent substance in experience; it is known through changing thoughts and objects and depends on consciousness for its appearance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனஸ் தனிப்பட்டு இராது?

units.claim_summary: Only the Self is said to stand independently, while body, senses, mind, and world are experienced in relation and therefore cannot be the absolute ground.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தனித்து நிற்பது ஆத்மாவே?

units.claim_summary: Electricity is used as an analogy for one unseen power enabling diverse devices, illustrating how one consciousness can appear through many bodies and minds without itself becoming many.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மின்ஸார உபமானம்?

units.claim_summary: Jivatman and Paramatman are distinguished at the empirical level while the teaching asks what, if anything, remains of that distinction when limiting adjuncts are removed.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பரமாத்ம – ஜீவாத்மாக்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Paramatman is presented as both cause of the universe and indwelling presence, joining cosmological lordship with the immediate consciousness within beings.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பரமாத்மா : ஜகத் காரணன், அந்தர்யாமி?

units.claim_summary: Ishvara or saguna Brahman is Brahman understood together with the cosmic causal power of maya and attributes suitable for devotion and explanation of the world.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வரன் அல்லது ஸகுண ப்ரஹ்மம்?

units.claim_summary: Vedantic use of the word Ishvara does not refer exclusively to the sectarian deity Shiva; it denotes the supreme Lord and can be expressed through different divine names and forms.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வேதாந்த ‘ஈச்வரன்’ சிவனல்ல?

units.claim_summary: Worship of Ishvara disciplines the mind through surrender and concentration and prepares it for knowledge, even though worship presupposes a provisional distinction between devotee and Lord.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈச்வர உபாஸனை?

units.claim_summary: Truth can be investigated from the individual side by asking who the jiva is and from the cosmic side by asking what the world’s cause is; Vedanta brings both inquiries to one ground.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸத்ய ஆராய்ச்சி – ஜீவ கோணத்திலும், ஜகத் கோணத்திலும்?

units.claim_summary: The Self of the individual and the Self associated with Ishvara are examined through their limiting conditions, with Advaita locating their apparent difference in those adjuncts rather than in consciousness itself.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜீவ ஆத்மா, ஈச்வர ஆத்மா?

units.claim_summary: Dvaita and Vishishtadvaita retain a real distinction or qualified relation between jiva and Paramatman, and their positions are described comparatively rather than collapsed into Advaita.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about த்வைத – விசிஷ்டாத்வைதங்களில் ஜீவாத்ம – பரமாத்மாக்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Any relation requires two terms, so theories that posit an eternal relation between jiva and God thereby retain a form of duality that Advaita ultimately seeks to transcend.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தொடர்புகொண்ட இரண்டு வஸ்துக்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The term Paramatman is preferred to “Ishvaratman” because the discourse wants to point beyond the Lord conceived with attributes to the supreme Self that is not limited by a role.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘ஈச்வராத்மா’வுக்குப் பதில் ஏன் ‘பரமாத்மா’??

units.claim_summary: Several core Advaita claims are restated together: Brahman alone is absolute, plurality is dependent appearance, and the jiva’s true nature is not different from that absolute reality.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அத்வைதக் கொள்கைகளில் சில?

units.claim_summary: The empirical jiva cannot simply become the cosmic Ishvara as one individual gaining divine office; liberation is knowledge that the underlying consciousness was never limited to the individual ego.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஜீவன் ஈசனாக முடியாது?

units.claim_summary: Even in dualistic experience the jiva is not independent of Ishvara, because existence, order, and the possibility of devotion are presented as dependent on the Lord.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about த்வைத ஜீவனுக்கு ஈசன் தொடர்புண்டு?

units.claim_summary: Ishvara’s association with maya is distinguished from the jiva’s association with ignorance and the inner instrument, explaining why the two appear different despite a common consciousness ground.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஈசன் – ஜீவன்; அவித்யை – அந்தஃகரணம்?

units.claim_summary: Dvaita liberation is described as freedom from material nature while retaining the soul’s distinct relation to God, in contrast with Advaita’s claim of identity with Brahman.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about த்வைத ‘மோக்ஷ’மும் ப்ரக்ருதி (மாயை)யும்?

units.claim_summary: From an Advaita perspective, any eternally retained duality leaves some logical possibility of limitation or dependence, which is why nondual freedom is presented as the only absolute end of suffering.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about த்வைத ருசிக்குத் துன்பம் தவிர்க்கவொண்ணாதது?

units.claim_summary: Spiritual practice is compared to a process of purification: the mind must be repeatedly cleaned of accumulated tendencies before the truth it reflects can be recognized clearly.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பரிசுத்தி செய்துகொள்ளும் பணி?

units.claim_summary: A linguistic inquiry into the terms Paramatman and jivatman is used to show how ordinary grammar itself reflects a contrast between supreme and limited selfhood that philosophy must finally examine.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாஷை ஆராய்ச்சி : அதிலும் பரமாத்ம – ஜீவாத்மா?

units.claim_summary: Cleaning a vessel is used as an analogy for sadhana: practice does not manufacture the Self but removes the impurities that prevent the mind from reflecting it clearly.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாத்திரம் தேய்ப்பதுபோல?

units.claim_summary: The image of separating impurity from grain or powder is used to illustrate discrimination between the Self and the admixture of body-mind tendencies mistaken for it.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘ரவை ஸல்லா’ உவமை?

units.claim_summary: After cultivating good qualities, the aspirant must guard against their contamination by ego, possessiveness, or desire for recognition, because virtue can itself become a new attachment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நல்லதில் கெட்டது கலக்காமலிருக்க?

units.claim_summary: Different names for love describe varied relational expressions, but the underlying movement is self-expansion beyond narrow ego and therefore has spiritual value.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அன்பின் பல பெயர்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Bhakti is characterized as love directed to the divine with humility, dependence, and longing, not merely intellectual belief or ritual correctness.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பக்தி – அன்பின் லக்ஷணம்?

units.claim_summary: Devotion can culminate in Advaitic liberation because intense love weakens egoic separateness until the devotee’s distinction from the beloved is no longer experienced as ultimate.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பக்தியால் அத்வைத முக்தி?

units.claim_summary: Love is necessary on the path because dry control or analysis alone may not melt the ego; devotion gives the mind a positive, emotionally powerful direction toward self-transcendence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பக்தி – அன்பின் அவசியம்?

units.claim_summary: Realized Advaitins are described as receiving nondual realization through the grace of their chosen deity, so devotion is presented as compatible with and capable of culminating in Advaitic knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அநுபூதி பெற்றோர் விஷயம்?

units.claim_summary: When some realized teachers appear to have bypassed preliminary karma and devotion, the discourse explains this through prior-birth spiritual maturity and the Gita model of the yoga-bhrashta resuming an unfinished path.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அநுபூதி பெற்றோர் விஷயம்?

units.claim_summary: For people who have not attained realization, the safe path remains disciplined dharma, devotion, self-control, and inquiry rather than imitation of exceptional jnanis.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நமக்கான வழி?

units.claim_summary: No genuine spiritual path should be condemned merely because its method differs, since different dispositions require different disciplines and all should be judged by whether they reduce ego and lead toward truth.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பிற மார்க்கத் தொடர்பு; எதையும் கண்டிக்கலாகாது?

units.claim_summary: As practice matures, discipline becomes increasingly natural rather than externally forced, because repeated right action and contemplation reshape the aspirant’s tendencies.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தன்னியல்பான ஸாதனை முதிர்வு?

units.claim_summary: Dharma is compared to medicine that restrains harmful impulses and purifies the mind even before the patient fully appreciates or enjoys the treatment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தர்ம மருந்து?

units.claim_summary: Advaita is wrongly accused of making ethics irrelevant; the discourse answers that nondual realization presupposes deep purification and cannot be invoked by an ego still governed by selfish desire.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தவறான குற்றச்சாட்டு?

units.claim_summary: For a true Advaitin dharma and adharma no longer bind in the ordinary way only because the doer-ego has ended, not because moral distinctions may be casually ignored before realization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தர்ம – அதர்மங்களும் அத்வைதியும்?

units.claim_summary: A jnani is said to stand beyond ordinary merit and demerit while remaining inwardly untouched by the bodily consequences conventionally attributed to prarabdha karma.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஞானியும் வினைப் பயனும்?

units.claim_summary: Competing Advaita explanations of whether prarabdha survives realization are examined, and the continued embodied life of a jnani is explained as evidence of liberation and as an instrument of benefit to others rather than as renewed personal bondage.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஞானியும் வினைப் பயனும்?

units.claim_summary: Exceptional conduct attributed to realized sages is explicitly denied as a license for ordinary aspirants: one must first abandon adharma, practice dharma, and only at advanced qualification transcend attachment to the distinction of dharma and adharma.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஞானியும் வினைப் பயனும்?

units.claim_summary: Dharma and love support one another: disciplined conduct limits selfish harm, while love gives positive warmth and universality to what would otherwise become rigid rule-following.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தர்மமும் அன்பும்?

units.claim_summary: Love is needed for the mind to loosen its self-protective hardness, because emotional surrender can dissolve attachments that abstract analysis leaves intact.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனம் பட்டுப்போக அன்பு தேவை?

units.claim_summary: Without a high spiritual aim, human capacities settle around immediate interests; keeping liberation or divine realization as the highest goal gives direction even to imperfect daily practice.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உயர் லக்ஷ்யமில்லாவிடில் உயர்நிலை ஸித்திப்பதில்லை?

units.claim_summary: Traditions in which divine or subtle powers trouble aspirants are treated as part of the inherited spiritual worldview and should be understood as attributed supernatural claims rather than independently verified facts.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தேவசக்திகளும் பீடிப்பதுண்டு?

units.claim_summary: Teachings of Tirumular and Tiruvalluvar are invoked to support self-restraint, compassion, and disciplined inner life as prerequisites for genuine spiritual progress.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருமூலர், திருவள்ளுவர் அறிவுரை?

units.claim_summary: The idea of nonduality should be remembered from the beginning as the direction of the path, while actual conduct must still respect the aspirant’s present dualistic stage and duties.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆரம்பத்திலிருந்தே அத்வைத நினைப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Spiritual progress encounters knots created by habit, fear, attachment, and ego, so difficulty in practice is expected and must be met by patience rather than treated as evidence that the goal is false.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கட்டவிழ்க்கும் கஷ்டங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The aspirant must eventually transcend attachment even to conventional goodness and merit, not by becoming immoral but by giving up the egoic ownership and reward-seeking that can cling to good action.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நல்லதற்கும் மேலே செல்க!?

units.claim_summary: Some degree of Self-inquiry is presented as necessary for everyone because without examining who acts and desires, religious practice can remain entirely outward and ego-centered.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்ம சிந்தனை அனைவர்க்கும் அவசியம்?

units.claim_summary: Questions about Self, mind, God, duty, and liberation should be investigated carefully rather than accepted as slogans, because Vedanta requires discriminative understanding as well as faith.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆலோசித்து அறிய வேண்டியவை?

units.claim_summary: Advaita’s metaphysical claim must be distinguished from the practitioner’s present empirical condition; asserting the highest truth verbally does not erase ordinary distinctions in lived conduct.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அத்வைத தத்வமும் நடப்பு நிலையும்?

units.claim_summary: The practical movement toward Advaita begins from ordinary dualistic life through duty, devotion, purification, concentration, and inquiry rather than by pretending the final realization has already occurred.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நடப்பு நிலையிலிருந்து அத்வைதத்துக்கு?

units.claim_summary: Shankara’s many devotional hymns are presented as evidence that Advaita and personal devotion are compatible stages and expressions of one spiritual life rather than mutually exclusive commitments.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆதிசங்கரரின் பக்தித் துதிகள்?

units.claim_summary: The Shatpadi Stotra is introduced as a compact devotional hymn in which Shankara prays to Vishnu for qualities that support liberation, making bhakti an explicit companion to Advaitic teaching.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஷட்பதீ ஸ்தோத்ரம்?

units.claim_summary: The hymn’s language is read through the analogy of vowel, consonant, and combined syllable to show how dependent individuality gains meaningful expression only in relation to the divine ground.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about உயிரும் மெய்யும் உயிர்மெய்யும்?

units.claim_summary: Sanskrit prosody is divided into syllable-counted vrtta and mora-counted jati meters, with sama, ardhasama, vishama, and Arya forms used to explain how metrical structure is classified.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இருவகைச் சந்தங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The Shatpadi hymn is scanned as Arya by explicit matra counts and then compared with the related Giti pattern, turning the preceding prosodic theory into a worked metrical analysis.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இருவகைச் சந்தங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Although known as Shatpadi, the hymn is organized as six principal verses whose compact form carries a complete progression of prayer from purification to refuge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆறு ச்லோகத் துதி?

units.claim_summary: The title Shatpadi is treated as a pun that can mean both “six-footed/six-versed” and “bee,” preparing the later image of the devotee as a bee seeking the lotus feet of the Lord.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சிலேடை மர்மம்?

units.claim_summary: The devotee’s requests are directed not toward ordinary possessions but toward humility, control of mind and senses, compassion, and release from samsara.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எதற்கு வேண்டுவது??

units.claim_summary: The prayer is interpreted as asking for precisely those inner transformations that divine grace is said to value, aligning the devotee’s wish with the spiritual purpose of worship.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பகவானின் கருத்து?

units.claim_summary: Even when a prayer uses language that could sound worldly, its legitimate meaning is read in the light of spiritual welfare rather than as a demand that God satisfy every temporal preference.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about லௌகிக ப்ரார்த்தனைக்கு ஸமாதானம்?

units.claim_summary: Failure of a particular prayer is not taken as evidence against God, because the tradition allows that divine response may differ from the petitioner’s limited judgment of what is beneficial.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரார்த்தனை ஈடேறாமையும் நாஸ்திகமும்?

units.claim_summary: Prayer for inner purification and liberation is distinguished from bargaining for external outcomes, because spiritual welfare cannot conflict with the ultimate purpose attributed to grace.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆத்ம ச்ரேயஸுக்கான ப்ரார்த்தனை?

units.claim_summary: Vishnu is invoked not only for worldly protection but also as the source of knowledge, showing that jnana is not confined to a sectarian association with one deity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஞானத்துக்கும் விஷ்ணு?

units.claim_summary: The prayer asks first for the mind to become properly oriented and disciplined, because an unsteady mind distorts both devotion and inquiry.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மனம் ஸரியாக?

units.claim_summary: Humility is treated as the chief requested virtue because pride reinforces separateness and prevents both surrender to God and receptivity to knowledge.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about முக்யப் பண்பு விநயமே?

units.claim_summary: Descriptions of Shankara’s disciples as humble bees drinking the nectar of his teaching are assembled from disciple and later literary testimony to connect scholarship with disciplined humility.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சங்கரரும், சிஷ்யர்களும், விநயமும்?

units.claim_summary: Shankara himself is presented as the stronger model of humility: despite supreme status he prays for removal of pride, and the lesson is extended to cultivating modesty from childhood before learning, wealth, power, or age harden ego.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சங்கரரும், சிஷ்யர்களும், விநயமும்?

units.claim_summary: A Sikh religious example is cited to show that humility before the divine and teacher is not confined to one Hindu school; the interreligious comparison remains illustrative rather than a claim of doctrinal identity.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸிக்கியர் மதத்தில்?

units.claim_summary: Two forms of humility are distinguished: deliberate lowering of ego through discipline and the effortless absence of self-importance that follows deeper realization.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இருவித அடக்கம்?

units.claim_summary: The mirage illustrates how appearance can be experienced without possessing the reality attributed to it, providing a familiar analogy for Vedantic accounts of the world’s dependent appearance.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கானல் நீர்?

units.claim_summary: The desert-mirage analogy is refined so that illusion is not confused with sheer nonexistence: an appearance requires a real basis even though its interpreted object is mistaken.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பாலைவன உவமையின் பொருத்தம்?

units.claim_summary: The contrast between Sahara desert and ocean develops the mirage metaphor by opposing thirst-producing appearance with the fullness symbolized by the boundless divine reality.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸஹாரா – ஸாகரம்?

units.claim_summary: The prayer seeks not only personal release but also welfare for the world, presenting genuine spiritual aspiration as compatible with compassion for others still in samsara.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தனது உய்வோடு உலகமும் உய்ய?

units.claim_summary: The request to be carried to the farther shore uses the ocean-crossing metaphor for liberation, with divine grace functioning as the means of passage beyond samsara.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “அக்கரை அடைவிப்பாய்!”?

units.claim_summary: The hymn’s simple and sweet diction is praised because profound spiritual prayer need not depend on technical philosophical language to transform the mind.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இனிய எளிய ச்லோகம்?

units.claim_summary: Lakshmi and the lotus are invoked through Vishnu imagery to connect beauty, auspiciousness, purity, and divine grace within the hymn’s devotional symbolism.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருமகளும் தாமரையும்?

units.claim_summary: The Lord’s feet are associated with the source of Ganga, making surrender at those feet a symbolic return to the purifying source celebrated in sacred geography and mythology.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கங்கை சுரக்கும் திருவடி?

units.claim_summary: The divine feet are prayed to as removing samsaric suffering and granting enduring bliss, shifting devotion from temporary relief toward final spiritual freedom.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸம்ஸாரம் நீக்கி ஸதாநந்தம் அருளும் அடி?

units.claim_summary: The verses form an antadi-like chain in which the end of one thought leads into the next, so poetic structure mirrors the continuity of the spiritual argument.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அதிசய அந்தாதி?

units.claim_summary: The hymn’s verbal linkage is accompanied by conceptual linkage: each request develops from the previous one toward deeper surrender and liberation rather than standing as an unrelated list.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கருத்திலும் தொடர்ச்சி காட்டும் ச்லோகம்?

units.claim_summary: Wordplay on repeated forms of bhavati is used to pray that direct vision of the Lord remove the residual taste for samsara, echoing the Gita’s claim that higher vision displaces lower craving.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தர்சனத்தால் ஸம்ஸார நீக்கம்?

units.claim_summary: Shankara’s use of Ishvara and Parameshvara for Vishnu is presented as evidence of Shiva-Vishnu non-difference within Advaita rather than exclusive sectarian ownership of those titles.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருமாலுக்கு ஈச்வர சப்தம்?

units.claim_summary: Vishnu’s avatar traditions are interpreted as forms of protection centered ultimately on preserving dharma, and Shankara’s nonsectarian usage allows the same supreme lordship to be expressed through Vishnu.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அவதாரங்கள்?

units.claim_summary: The twelve principal names of Vishnu are connected with the Vaishnava forehead marks, showing how sacred names, body-marking, and daily remembrance reinforce one devotional discipline.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பன்னிரு நாமங்கள் : நெற்றிக்கிடும் நாமம்?

units.claim_summary: Damodara is explained through Krishna’s being bound by Yashoda and then philosophically as the one who contains all things, joining intimate bhakti narrative with a cosmic interpretation of the name.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தாமோதரன்?

units.claim_summary: Names such as Govinda, Keshava, Hrishikesha, and Damodara are interpreted through their devotional and philosophical meanings, with the Shatpadi deliberately drawing on this rich Vaishnava name tradition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about திருப்பெயர்களின் பொருள்?

units.claim_summary: Calling the Lord a “repository of qualities” is reconciled with nirguna Brahman by arguing that a realized Advaitin can delight in saguna forms without treating their distinction from the absolute as ultimately real.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நிர்குணமும் குணநிலயமும்?

units.claim_summary: Examples of Advaitin saints devoted to Krishna are used to show that intense saguna bhakti can coexist with nondual realization, because divine form may be relished without re-establishing ultimate duality.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about க்ருஷ்ண பக்தர்களான அத்வைதிகள்?

units.claim_summary: Govinda and Hara are singled out as especially powerful divine names in communal remembrance, with Govinda further associated with Krishna’s Govardhana narrative and the disciplining of Indra’s pride.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கோவிந்த – ஹர நாமச்சிறப்பு?

units.claim_summary: Andal’s “faultless Govinda” is interpreted as praise of Krishna’s completeness, using his narratives to distinguish apparent dramatic deficiency from the plenitude attributed to the divine.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “குறைவொன்றுமில்லாத கோவிந்தா”?

units.claim_summary: Govinda is significant as both a divine name and the name of Shankara’s guru, allowing devotion to God and reverence for the teacher to converge in one expression of surrender.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about குரு – தெய்வ ‘கோவிந்த’?

units.claim_summary: Calling Govinda the churning rod of the ocean of samsara presents divine grace as transforming the painful mixture of worldly life until the aspirant reaches the nectar-like freedom sought through spiritual maturation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பவக்கடல் கடையும் பகவத் மத்து!?

units.claim_summary: A small number of exemplary persons can preserve and renew a tradition when they embody it deeply, so cultural survival is not reduced to majority participation alone.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சில உதாரணர புருஷர் போதும்?

units.claim_summary: The hymn’s central aim is summarized as release from the distress of samsara through humility, devotion, divine vision, and surrender rather than acquisition of worldly benefits.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about துதியின் ஸாரம் : ஸம்ஸாரத் துன்ப நீக்கம்?

units.claim_summary: The recurrence of the hymn’s opening idea near its end creates formal closure and reinforces that the entire prayer returns to the removal of ego and bondage.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆதி வார்த்தை அந்தத்திலும்?

units.claim_summary: The concluding verse functions like a phalashruti yet remains a personal surrender, asking the Lord to accept and carry the devotee rather than merely promising external rewards for recitation.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about பலச்ருதி போன்ற சரணாகதி விண்ணப்பம்?

units.claim_summary: The six verses are compressed into six key expressions that trace the hymn’s spiritual movement from humility and mind-control through compassion and refuge to release.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஆறு ச்லோகமும் ஆறு வார்த்தையும்?

units.claim_summary: The “bee” meaning hidden in the title Shatpadi is finally resolved by identifying the devotee with a bee seeking the nectar of the Lord’s lotus feet, uniting the poem’s formal and devotional imagery.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ‘வண்டு’ப் புதிர் அவிழ்கிறது!?

units.claim_summary: The lives of great saints and scholars are used to argue that spiritual and intellectual greatness can stand above royal power because truth and renunciation need not depend on political favor.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அரசருக்கும் மேலே!?

units.claim_summary: A mahan is distinguished from a merely gifted poet: literary brilliance may coexist with ego, whereas spiritual greatness is measured by self-mastery and freedom from the need for recognition.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மஹான் – கவி வித்யாஸம்?

units.claim_summary: Stories of saints who disregard kings are presented as examples of independence from patronage, not as contempt for lawful authority but as refusal to subordinate dharma or truth to worldly power.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மன்னனைப் பொருட்படுத்தாத மஹான்கள்?

units.claim_summary: Renunciation of reward should be joined with a proper sense of dignity, because self-respect protects principle while pride converts that independence into another form of ego.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வைராக்கியமும் மான உணர்வும்?

units.claim_summary: The Kalidasa-Bhoja stories explore the tension between poetic genius, friendship, patronage, and royal expectation, showing why genuine art cannot always be commanded by a king.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காளிதாஸனும் போஜராஜனும்?

units.claim_summary: Kalidasa’s refusal to compose false praise of Bhoja is valued because poetic truth should not be sold to flatter power even when patronage and friendship are at stake.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காளிதாஸன் மறுப்பும் அதன் சிறப்பும்?

units.claim_summary: The disguise episode shows patron and poet testing one another indirectly, using wit and altered identity to reveal motives that ordinary courtly roles might conceal.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மாறு வேஷம்?

units.claim_summary: Traditional stories about famous poets may not meet modern historical standards, but they can still preserve moral and cultural insights if kept distinct from claims of verified biography.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மரபுவழிக் கதைகளும் ஆராய்ச்சியும்?

units.claim_summary: The Kamban-Kulottunga tradition is used to show a poet’s willingness to leave royal favor when dignity and literary independence are threatened.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கம்பரும் குலோத்துங்கனும்?

units.claim_summary: Friendship between poet and king can turn into hostility when status, expectation, or pride enters the relationship, illustrating how attachment can corrupt even genuine mutual regard.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நட்பு பகையாவதன் நுட்பம்?

units.claim_summary: Kamban and Kalidasa are compared as towering poets whose independence from kings is remembered alongside their literary genius rather than as a reason to rank one tradition against another.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கம்பர் – காளிதாஸன் ஒப்பீடு?

units.claim_summary: The story of the Chera ruler serving in Kamban’s circle dramatizes the idea that devotion to learning and poetry can invert ordinary status, placing a king in willing service to a poet.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சோழ ஸபையில் “அடைப்பைக்கார”ச் சேரன்?

units.claim_summary: Kamban’s greatness is located not only in poetic ability but also in nobility of character, gratitude, courage, and the capacity to place truth above courtly advantage.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கம்பரின் உயர் பண்பு?

units.claim_summary: Two scholars nicknamed “Kutti” are introduced as examples of intellectual courage and independence whose small appellation contrasts playfully with the scale of their learning.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about இரண்டு “குட்டி”கள்?

units.claim_summary: Poetry in praise of a ruler is not rejected in itself; it becomes legitimate when praise corresponds to real virtue rather than functioning as purchased flattery.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அரசனைப் போற்றும் கவிதை?

units.claim_summary: Mutual praise between a ruler and a gifted child-poet is presented as beautiful when each recognizes the other without servility, showing that honor can flow in both directions across status.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மன்னரும் குழந்தையும்: பரஸ்பரப் பாராட்டு?

units.claim_summary: Kutti Kavi’s satire of Pratapa Simha is used as a case in which literary ridicule becomes moral criticism intended to correct a ruler rather than merely entertain or humiliate him.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ப்ரதாப ஸிம்ஹனும் குட்டிக் கவியும்?

units.claim_summary: Mahisha Satakam praises the buffalo ironically in order to expose corrupt patronage and scholars who sell learning, using satire to shame a court that rewards sycophancy over merit.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about எருமைத்துதி?

units.claim_summary: When the king reforms after the satire, the poet preserves the work as evidence that fearless literary criticism can benefit a whole polity and need not be suppressed once its immediate target changes.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நாட்டைக் காத்த கவி?

units.claim_summary: The young scholar’s victory over a renowned Bengal logician is narrated as an example of precocious learning and confidence, a biographical tradition that remains subject to historical verification.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வங்க வித்வானை வென்ற வாலிபர்?

units.claim_summary: Kutti Sastri’s refusal to alter Vedic observance for Serfoji’s convenience is praised as independence of dharma from royal pressure, even at the cost of leaving the ruler’s domain.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about சரபோஜிக்கு பணியாத சாஸ்த்ரியார்?

units.claim_summary: Loyalty to a patron in misfortune is valued above attachment to prosperity, while the scholar’s later independence under another ruler shows that friendship need not become servility.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about ஸ்நேஹத்திலும் சிறந்த சாஸ்த்ரியார்?

units.claim_summary: Kutti Sastri declines the Mysore king’s request for a grand sacrifice because he judges proper performance impracticable, placing ritual conscience above royal favor and ceremonial prestige.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மைஸூர் மன்னருக்கு மறுதலிப்பு?

units.claim_summary: The scholar’s connection with the Kanchi Math is invoked to make his combination of independence, courtesy, and concern for others an inherited example for the teaching community.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about “நம் பந்து”?

units.claim_summary: Self-respect can occasionally spill into pride even among great poets and scholars; such lapses should be contextualized within their larger virtues rather than used either to idealize or dismiss them wholesale.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about அதுவும் ஓர் அழகு!?

units.claim_summary: When human debate cannot decide literary superiority, traditional stories place the matter before the deity, presenting divine adjudication as a hagiographic motif rather than a historically testable procedure.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about தெய்வத் தீர்ப்புக் கோருவது?

units.claim_summary: The first Kalidasa legend portrays the Goddess judging rival poets and then telling the impatient Kalidasa that he is not separate from her, making divine wisdom and aesthetic rasa the source of his poetic power rather than personal ownership.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காளிதாஸனும் அம்பிகையும்?

units.claim_summary: A second Kalidasa-Bhavabhuti weighing legend portrays the Goddess deliberately reversing an apparent victory to humble Kalidasa and console Bhavabhuti; Kalidasa recognizes the correction as grace rather than reacting with resentment.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காளிதாஸனும் அம்பிகையும்?

units.claim_summary: The reconciliation of the rival poets and Kalidasa’s later self-effacing posture are used as the moral conclusion: true poetic greatness matures into humility rather than competition and pride.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about காளிதாஸனும் அம்பிகையும்?

units.claim_summary: Avvaiyar’s encounter with Kamban is used to puncture poetic arrogance through wit, teaching that extraordinary talent still requires humility before other forms of wisdom.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about கம்பரும் அவ்வையும்?

units.claim_summary: The Villiputtur-Arunagirinathar tradition portrays extreme poetic pride and cruel contest as being overcome by superior spiritual-literary power, a hagiographic story that condemns learned arrogance rather than endorsing violence.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about வில்லிப்புத்தூராரும் அருணகிரிநாதரும்?

units.claim_summary: The encounter between Nilakantha Dikshita and Mahadeva Sastri shows one scholar’s pride being checked by another’s deeper learning, and the resulting correction is used to teach that even great intellects grow through humility.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about நீலகண்டரும் மஹாதேவரும்*?

units.claim_summary: A Shiva hymn’s statement that even deformity can become praiseworthy in association with the divine is used to illustrate how devotion can transform the meaning of what would otherwise be regarded as a defect.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about விகாரமும் ஏற்றம் பெறுகிறது!?

units.claim_summary: Hanuman is presented as the model of perfectly controlled power: although endowed with the speed associated with wind and mind, he directs body, senses, learning, courage, and devotion wholly toward Rama rather than toward restless self-expression.
question_intents: What proposition does this teaching develop about மாருதி மஹிமை?
